transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood CSM), Sam Rivera (Redwood SE), Alex Monroe (Greenbridge Head of Engineering), Dr. Sarah Wu (Greenbridge CTO), Riley Chen (Greenbridge SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. Quick round intros — I'm Jordan, AE on the account, Priya is your CSM, Sam is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Priya: Hi all, excited to kick this off — we'll run through the plan and next steps.
[00:12] Alex: Thanks Jordan, yeah Sarah and Riley, we're glad to be here. We're trying to move fast Q1, so want to get the onboarding path clarified.
[00:20] Jordan: Awesome. High level agenda: onboarding timeline, infra & network needs for Private/Dedicated, security and compliance checklist, perf benchmark plan, then actions. Sound good?
[00:28] Alex: Yep.
[00:31] Sam: Quick note — I might chime in technical details around VPC peering, KMS/HSM, and the benchmark.
[00:36] Dr. Sarah: Perfect. We have questions around data residency and audit logs up front.
[00:40] Jordan: Great. So first, onboarding plan — Priya, can you run the sequence?
[00:45] Priya: Sure. Step one: access & accounts — we'll need SAML metadata for SSO, and a list of users/roles. Step two: infra provisioning — if you pick Dedicated or Private we'll need network CIDR ranges, egress rules, and firewall exceptions. Step three: test traffic & benchmarks — Sam will help you run a perf test. Final step: go-live and SLA review. We'll attach the onboarding checklist after the call.
[01:10] Alex: On SSO, we use Okta. We'll share metadata. One of our requirements is RBAC and fine-grained audit logs for the token-level access.
[01:20] Priya: Yep, Redwood supports SAML and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC roles are configurable. Audit logs — we can route them to your SIEM and provide retention settings.
[01:30] Riley: How detailed are the audit logs? We need token-level request traces for compliance.
[01:35] Sam: You can get per-request traces and token-cost breakdowns from the Console. There is an option to export logs to S3 or to your logging endpoint. Small caveat — depending on whether you go Hosted vs Dedicated, retention windows differ by plan but we can set up long-term exports.
[01:50] Dr. Sarah: Good. Next, network: we plan to keep things in our VPC. For Dedicated, will Redwood provide a customer VPC or do we peer?
[02:00] Sam: For Redwood Dedicated we do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your cloud. There's a Private deployment option too for air-gapped environments. For peering we'll need the CIDR, allowed ports — usually HTTPS to our endpoints and a few control-plane ports. We'll send a network spec.
[02:18] Alex: Ok. We may prefer VPC peering to avoid public egress, but we need the exact port numbers and ACL rules.
[02:25] Sam: Absolutely — I'll attach the network appendix. Also note: KV cache and streaming endpoints have sticky IPs for Dedicated pools; you'll want to allow them.
[02:36] Jordan: Cost conversation — Alex noted you want predictable latency. Do you have a target latency and QPS?
[02:44] Alex: We're aiming for 95th percentile < 120ms for simple completion requests at baseline 100 QPS, spiking to 300 QPS during peaks.
[02:55] Sam: That profile typically maps to Dedicated capacity. We can size a pool and run benchmarks — quantization and batching settings will affect token cost and latency.
[03:07] Riley: What's the difference in data handling between Hosted and Dedicated? We need assurance client data isn't used in model training and is isolated.
[03:15] Priya: Redwood's contract terms for Dedicated include data isolation and a no-training clause; we also offer Private with customer-managed control plane for stricter needs. I'll attach the security pack (SOC2, ISOs) and the data processing addendum.
[03:30] Dr. Sarah: We'll need the SOC2 report and an explanation of your key management — KMS or HSM?
[03:36] Sam: We integrate with AWS KMS and have HSM options for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can bring your keys or use Redwood-managed keys depending on contract.
[03:46] Alex: Good, send the SOC2 and a short note on HSM capabilities.
[03:50] Priya: Will do.
[03:53] Jordan: On timeline — if you want Q1 go-live, I'd recommend we start access and network this month, run benchmarks mid-December and finalize contract by late December. Does that align?
[04:05] Alex: That lines up with our procurement window. Procurement folks expect a timeline for IT and security review.
[04:10] Riley: Also want to test some of our edge prompts and dataset redaction. Sam, can you help with a test harness?
[04:16] Sam: Yes — we have a sample perf harness and a prompt set runner. We'll need a token-limited sandbox account and some sample traffic.
[04:24] Alex: We'll prepare a small dataset and share. Any docs for the harness?
[04:27] Sam: I'll share the runbook link after the call.
[04:30] Jordan: Competitor question — are you evaluating others?
[04:33] Alex: Yeah briefly. We're looking at OpenAI and Anthropic for model quality, and we also talked to some infra folks.
[04:40] Jordan: Cool, okay. Pricing — we'll send both Hosted and Dedicated TCOs. For Dedicated we show committed monthly capacity with burst options.
[04:49] Dr. Sarah: Curious about quantization & quality tradeoffs. If we quantize to 4-bit, do we see regressions on our prompts?
[04:56] Sam: There's always a model-specific delta. We recommend running a small eval set; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload and flag regressions. We'll include that in the benchmark.
[05:08] Riley: Any firewall requirements for the benchmark nodes?
[05:11] Sam: Nope beyond peering and port allowances; the test harness can be run from inside your VPC if you'd prefer.
[05:17] Alex: Great. Last: procurement & contract. Who on your side handles enterprise contracts?
[05:22] Priya: I can coordinate, but Jordan will be the AE handling pricing and legal. We'll loop in our legal and security teams.
[05:28] Jordan: Yep. We'll provide the security pack and a standard MSA; we can support an SOW for implementation.
[05:33] Alex: Perfect. Any blockers right now?
[05:35] Priya: None from our side — just need SSO metadata and network CIDRs to start provisioning.
[05:40] Riley: We'll send SAML metadata and CIDR by end of day tomorrow.
[05:44] Sam: I'll follow up with the network appendix and the perf runbook links.
[05:48] Jordan: Ok quick recap and actions — Priya will send checklist, Sam will schedule the technical deep-dive and perf run, Jordan to send pricing/quote, Alex to share SSO and compliance contact.
[05:58] Alex: Thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
[06:01] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches (e.g., "Redwood dedi—dedicated" shows up as "red wood dedi" in auto text). References shared: onboarding checklist (link sent by Priya after call), security pack (link), perf runbook (Sam to share).
